condition: suspected acute appendicitis presenting with sharp severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain
level_rationale: Acute sharp severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain today in a 22-year-old man indicates suspected acute appendicitis requiring immediate emergency department surgical and imaging evaluation, whereas mild lower belly bloating 4 hours after eating a big meal leaves no peritoneal or systemic red flags and is appropriate for home self-care or over-the-counter simethicone.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain young-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 verb-frame by clinical/everyday terminology crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-case postprandial lower-belly bloating self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (22-year-old man, eating a large meal 4 hours ago, and sharp severe right lower abdominal pain today) with a 1-word span difference (16 vs 17 words) and 8 shared trailing tokens ('today so I need to go to the'). Swapping only f3 to mild bloating in the lower belly stays inside the post-meal GI context while shifting care from ER (level 4) to home self-care (level 1) with zero residual red flags and zero stated negatives.
